title: A 'header-list' header matches a consumer that frames the list another way.
why: behavioural spec 'header-list' (ADR 0082 decision 2): the engine's http:list admits a header whose field lines, joined with commas, split into the elements, so a consumer that sends 'application/json,text/plain' on one line with no space matches a header declared as the two elements. Written as a plain value, the same request would fail: the line is not 'application/json, text/plain'. One variant, since the operator contributes no dimension.

interaction.description: an order list for a client that accepts two types
